title: Twisted-arrow site presentation of internal group actions on module sheaves
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(C,J)$ be a $\mathcal V$-small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $K:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Grp}$ be a sheaf of groups with $\mathcal V$-small values. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative unital rings on $C$, with $\mathcal V$-small values. Give $R$ the trivial $K$-action. A $K$-equivariant $R$-module sheaf is a sheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with natural operations $K(U)\times M(U)\to M(U)$ satisfying the group-action laws and linearity in $M(U)$; morphisms commute with these operations.

Define $C_K$ to have the objects of $C$, arrows $(f,a):V\to U$ with $f:V\to U$ in $C$ and $a\in K(V)$, identities $(1,1)$, and composition
$$(f,a)\circ(g,b)=(f\circ g,b\,g^*a).$$
Use the covering families $\{(f_i,a_i):U_i\to U\}$ for which $\{f_i:U_i\to U\}$ is a $J$-covering family. These families define a precoverage on the small category $C_K$. Singleton isomorphism families belong to this precoverage, and every such covering family admits covering pullbacks along every arrow, for some choice of pullbacks as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Equip $C_K$ with the Grothendieck topology generated by this precoverage. Explicitly, a sieve $S$ on $U$ is covering exactly when the base sieve $S_1=\{f:V\to U\mid(f,1)\in S\}$ is covering for the Grothendieck topology generated by $J$. The image precoverage is not asserted to satisfy composition by $\operatorname{Presieve.bind}$; the site used below is the generated Grothendieck site. The presheaf $R_K$ given by $R_K(U)=R(U)$ and $R_K(f,a)=f^*$ is a sheaf of commutative rings on this site. There is an additive equivalence from $K$-equivariant $R$-module sheaves to $\operatorname{Mod}(R_K)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] sending $M$ to the same section modules with restriction $m\mapsto a\cdot f^*m$ along $(f,a)$; its inverse restricts to $(f,1)$ and recovers $a\cdot m$ from $(1_U,a)$.

For an equivariant presheaf of $R$-modules, restriction to the arrows $(f,1)$ identifies its module sheafification on $C_K$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] with its module sheafification on $C$, with the induced $K$-action. In particular, forgetting the $K$-action creates kernels and cokernels: the underlying kernel is the sectionwise kernel and the underlying cokernel is the sheafification on $C$ of the sectionwise cokernel. A module sheaf on $C_K$ is zero if and only if its restriction to $C$ is zero.

proof.text: First construct the category. For composable $(f,a),(g,b),(h,c)$, both associations have underlying arrow $fgh$ and label $c\,h^*b\,(gh)^*a$, since restriction in $K$ is a group homomorphism. The two identity equations follow from $f^*1=1$. The arrow $(1_U,a)$ is invertible with inverse $(1_U,a^{-1})$. The objects and arrows are $\mathcal V$-small: the latter are the dependent union, over pairs of objects and base arrows $f:V\to U$, of the small sets $K(V)$. These are direct verifications of the category and size conditions, without any representability hypothesis on $K$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written categorical input: category laws and size

proof.text: Here is an explicit pullback, needed for the site axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For $(f,a):V\to U$ and $(g,b):W\to U$, choose $P=V\times_UW$ in $C$, with projections $p,q$. In $C_K$ use $(p,1)$ and $(q,e)$, where $e=p^*a\,(q^*b)^{-1}$. Their composites have label $p^*a$. A cone $(u,c):T\to V$, $(v,d):T\to W$ satisfies $fu=gv$ and $c\,u^*a=d\,v^*b$. Its unique factor is $(t,c):T\to P$, where $pt=u$, $qt=v$: the second projected label is $c\,t^*e=d$. The first projection forces both $t$ and the label, proving uniqueness. Thus these are actual pullbacks; for $a=b=1$ both projections have label $1$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written categorical input: explicit pullback calculation

proof.text: The proposed precoverage contains singleton isomorphism covers: projection sends inverses to inverses, and the base site has isomorphism covers [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For a covering family and an arrow $(g,b)$, apply the base covering-pullback axiom to its indexed underlying base family. The pullbacks of step 2, formed using precisely that choice of base pullbacks, have covering underlying arrows to the source of $(g,b)$. This proves existence of covering pullbacks, not closure under all choices. Do not infer bind composition: distinct labels over the same base arrow may choose different covering refinements, and their union need not be a base cover. Instead take the generated Grothendieck topology. For every sieve $S$, membership of $(f,a)$ is equivalent to membership of $(f,1)$ by precomposition with the source isomorphisms $(1,a)$ and $(1,a^{-1})$. Thus $S\mapsto S_1$ identifies twisted sieves with base sieves and preserves maximal sieves, pullbacks, and the local-character condition. Under this identification a sieve generated by a prescribed family corresponds to the base sieve generated by its underlying family. Conversely every base covering family lifts to a normalized family. Transport the base Grothendieck topology and compare these generators in both directions: the generated topology on $C_K$ consists exactly of sieves with covering $S_1$. This is the Grothendieck site used below. Every prescribed family still normalizes by $(f_i,a_i)=(f_i,1)\circ(1_{U_i},a_i)$, so the subsequent matching-family and sheafification arguments are unchanged.

proof.text:
At the presheaf level send an equivariant module $M$ to $E(M)$ with $E(M)(f,a)(m)=a\cdot f^*m$. Naturality of the action gives
$$b\cdot g^*(a\cdot f^*m)=(b\,g^*a)\cdot(fg)^*m,$$
which is exactly contravariant functoriality with the stated composition order. These restrictions are semilinear over $R(f)$ because the action is linear. The identity action gives identities. On morphisms use the same component linear maps; their naturality for $(f,a)$ follows from restriction naturality and equivariance. This uses precisely the presheaf-module notion [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written categorical input: explicit extension of presheaves

proof.text: Conversely, for a presheaf $N$ of $R_K$-modules restrict along $(f,1)$ and put $a\cdot n=N(1_U,a)(n)$. The identity and composition laws give $1\cdot n=n$ and $a\cdot(b\cdot n)=(ab)\cdot n$: indeed $(1,b)\circ(1,a)=(1,ab)$ and $N$ is contravariant. Comparing $(1_U,a)\circ(f,1)=(f,f^*a)=(f,1)\circ(1_V,f^*a)$ gives restriction naturality. Semilinearity for $(1_U,a)$ is $R(U)$-linearity since its ring restriction is the identity. The factorization $(f,a)=(f,1)\circ(1_V,a)$ recovers every restriction of $N$. A natural transformation commutes with $(f,1)$ and $(1,a)$ exactly when it is restriction-natural and equivariant. Thus the two constructions are inverse on objects and morphisms, preserving addition of maps [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written categorical input: inverse and additivity

proof.text: For a normalized covering $\{(f_i,1)\}$, the pullback projections are normalized, by step 2. Hence the matching-family equalizer for $E(M)$ is exactly the matching-family equalizer for $M$ on $\{f_i\}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For an arbitrary cover, the source isomorphisms of step 3 and their induced pullback isomorphisms identify its matching diagram with the normalized one. Concretely its local section $n_i$ becomes $a_i^{-1}\cdot n_i$ on the normalized source; invertibility makes this a bijection of matching families and identifies their unique gluings. Thus $E(M)$ is a sheaf if and only if $M$ is one. Apply the same argument to $R$, whose action is trivial: $R_K(f,a)=f^*$ is functorial and $R_K$ is a ring sheaf. The inverse presheaf constructions of steps 4--5 therefore restrict to the claimed additive equivalence of module-sheaf categories.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written categorical input: matching-family calculation, including the ring sheaf

proof.text: Let $P$ now be an equivariant presheaf of $R$-modules on $C$, and let $A=P^\#$ be its ordinary module sheafification. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] its underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification; [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] identifies its underlying set sheaf and unit with set sheafification. Set sheafification preserves finite products [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]. Sheafify the natural set map $K\times P\to P$. Since $K$ is already a sheaf, this produces a map $K\times A\to A$ compatible with the unit $P\to A$. Its unit and associativity identities are the sheafifications of the original identities on $P$ and $K\times K\times P$. Its additivity and scalar-linearity identities are obtained in exactly the same way from the two equal maps on $K\times P\times P$ and $K\times R\times P$, respectively. Product preservation identifies their sheafifications with the corresponding products involving $A$, $K$ and $R$, since $K,R$ are sheaves. Thus all the required laws hold, and the extended action is unique because maps from the sheafification of $K\times P$ to the sheaf $A$ are determined by their composites with its unit.

source.place: Tags 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures); module sheafification is Tag 03CY in sites-modules.tex

proof.text: If $Q$ is an equivariant module sheaf and $v:P\to Q$ an equivariant presheaf map, the module-sheafification adjunction [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives a unique $R$-linear extension $v^\#:A\to Q$. It is equivariant: the two maps $K\times A\to Q$ expressing equivariance are equal after composition with $K\times P\to K\times A$, by equivariance of $v$. This last map is a set-sheafification unit by product preservation [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] and the underlying-set identification [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], so its universal property forces equality. Thus $A$ with the induced action is the reflection of $P$ into equivariant sheaves, with the same unit and underlying module sheafification.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), combined with Sites Tags 00WJ and 00YR

proof.text: Apply the equivalences of steps 4--6 to this reflection. For every $R_K$-module sheaf $N$, maps $E(P)\to N$ correspond to equivariant presheaf maps $P\to E^{-1}N$, which by step 8 extend uniquely to maps $A\to E^{-1}N$, hence to maps $E(A)\to N$. Therefore $E(P)\to E(A)$ has precisely the module-sheafification universal property on $C_K$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The canonical isomorphism from the sheafification of $E(P)$ to $E(A)$ is the unique one commuting with the unit. Restriction along $(f,1)$ is consequently the asserted sheafification comparison, natural in $P$; equivariance is part of the same isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03CY: uniqueness of the reflector, applied to the explicit equivalences

proof.text: For an equivariant map $M\to N$, its sectionwise kernel is stable under $K(U)$ since the map is equivariant. It is the underlying kernel sheaf on $C$ and has the kernel universal property among equivariant maps by restricting their images. The sectionwise cokernel $P(U)=N(U)/\operatorname{im}M(U)$ inherits the linear $K(U)$-action and restriction maps. Its module sheafification on $C$, with the action of step 7, is the equivariant cokernel: maps killing $M$ factor uniquely first through the quotient presheaf and then, equivariantly by step 8, through its sheafification. The formulas agree with the ordinary module kernels and cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so forgetting creates both. Finally the equivalence changes no section modules: a module sheaf on $C_K$ has zero restriction exactly when every section module is zero, which is exactly the zero module sheaf on $C_K$. This also covers the trivial group, the zero ring, and objects admitting empty covers.

statement_change.what: The image precoverage need not satisfy the bind composition clause of the recorded IsSiteForCoverings dependency. Counterexample: the Boolean lattice {0,a,b,1} as a category with all singleton presieves covering, and a constant sheaf of groups with distinct x,y. The twisted presieve {(id_1,x),(id_1,y)} is covering; refine its first arrow by the singleton {(a→1,1)} and its second by {(b→1,1)}. Its bind projects to the two-arrow {a→1,b→1}, which is not a singleton and hence is not a prescribed J-cover. The same repetition issue can produce infinite unions for finite jointly-surjective profinite coverings and infinite groups. Replace the false presieve-site assertion by isomorphism covers, existence of covering pullbacks, and the explicit generated Grothendieck topology. This retains exactly the sheaf category and all subsequent assertions; it changes no blueprint unit statement (this node is agent-formulated categorical input).

old_proof.text: First construct the category. For composable $(f,a),(g,b),(h,c)$, both associations have underlying arrow $fgh$ and label $c\,h^*b\,(gh)^*a$, since restriction in $K$ is a group homomorphism. The two identity equations follow from $f^*1=1$. The arrow $(1_U,a)$ is invertible with inverse $(1_U,a^{-1})$. The objects and arrows are $\mathcal V$-small: the latter are the dependent union, over pairs of objects and base arrows $f:V\to U$, of the small sets $K(V)$. These are direct verifications of the category and size conditions, without any representability hypothesis on $K$.

old_proof.text: Here is an explicit pullback, needed for the site axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For $(f,a):V\to U$ and $(g,b):W\to U$, choose $P=V\times_UW$ in $C$, with projections $p,q$. In $C_K$ use $(p,1)$ and $(q,e)$, where $e=p^*a\,(q^*b)^{-1}$. Their composites have label $p^*a$. A cone $(u,c):T\to V$, $(v,d):T\to W$ satisfies $fu=gv$ and $c\,u^*a=d\,v^*b$. Its unique factor is $(t,c):T\to P$, where $pt=u$, $qt=v$: the second projected label is $c\,t^*e=d$. The first projection forces both $t$ and the label, proving uniqueness. Thus these are actual pullbacks; for $a=b=1$ both projections have label $1$.

old_proof.text: The proposed coverings satisfy the three site axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. An isomorphism in $C_K$ has an underlying isomorphism in $C$, so its singleton covers. Composites of covering families cover because their underlying base families do. Pulling back a covering along $(g,b)$ gives the pullbacks just calculated; the arrows to its source $W$ have underlying maps $q:U_i\times_UW\to W$, a covering in $C$. This proves base-change stability. For later use, every $(f_i,a_i)$ equals $(f_i,1)\circ(1_{U_i},a_i)$: every cover is isomorphic, by invertible arrows on its sources, to its normalized cover with labels $1$.

old_proof.text:
At the presheaf level send an equivariant module $M$ to $E(M)$ with $E(M)(f,a)(m)=a\cdot f^*m$. Naturality of the action gives
$$b\cdot g^*(a\cdot f^*m)=(b\,g^*a)\cdot(fg)^*m,$$
which is exactly contravariant functoriality with the stated composition order. These restrictions are semilinear over $R(f)$ because the action is linear. The identity action gives identities. On morphisms use the same component linear maps; their naturality for $(f,a)$ follows from restriction naturality and equivariance. This uses precisely the presheaf-module notion [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

old_proof.text: Conversely, for a presheaf $N$ of $R_K$-modules restrict along $(f,1)$ and put $a\cdot n=N(1_U,a)(n)$. The identity and composition laws give $1\cdot n=n$ and $a\cdot(b\cdot n)=(ab)\cdot n$: indeed $(1,b)\circ(1,a)=(1,ab)$ and $N$ is contravariant. Comparing $(1_U,a)\circ(f,1)=(f,f^*a)=(f,1)\circ(1_V,f^*a)$ gives restriction naturality. Semilinearity for $(1_U,a)$ is $R(U)$-linearity since its ring restriction is the identity. The factorization $(f,a)=(f,1)\circ(1_V,a)$ recovers every restriction of $N$. A natural transformation commutes with $(f,1)$ and $(1,a)$ exactly when it is restriction-natural and equivariant. Thus the two constructions are inverse on objects and morphisms, preserving addition of maps [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

old_proof.text: For a normalized covering $\{(f_i,1)\}$, the pullback projections are normalized, by step 2. Hence the matching-family equalizer for $E(M)$ is exactly the matching-family equalizer for $M$ on $\{f_i\}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For an arbitrary cover, the source isomorphisms of step 3 and their induced pullback isomorphisms identify its matching diagram with the normalized one. Concretely its local section $n_i$ becomes $a_i^{-1}\cdot n_i$ on the normalized source; invertibility makes this a bijection of matching families and identifies their unique gluings. Thus $E(M)$ is a sheaf if and only if $M$ is one. Apply the same argument to $R$, whose action is trivial: $R_K(f,a)=f^*$ is functorial and $R_K$ is a ring sheaf. The inverse presheaf constructions of steps 4--5 therefore restrict to the claimed additive equivalence of module-sheaf categories.

old_proof.text: Let $P$ now be an equivariant presheaf of $R$-modules on $C$, and let $A=P^\#$ be its ordinary module sheafification. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] its underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification; [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] identifies its underlying set sheaf and unit with set sheafification. Set sheafification preserves finite products [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]. Sheafify the natural set map $K\times P\to P$. Since $K$ is already a sheaf, this produces a map $K\times A\to A$ compatible with the unit $P\to A$. Its unit and associativity identities are the sheafifications of the original identities on $P$ and $K\times K\times P$. Its additivity and scalar-linearity identities are obtained in exactly the same way from the two equal maps on $K\times P\times P$ and $K\times R\times P$, respectively. Product preservation identifies their sheafifications with the corresponding products involving $A$, $K$ and $R$, since $K,R$ are sheaves. Thus all the required laws hold, and the extended action is unique because maps from the sheafification of $K\times P$ to the sheaf $A$ are determined by their composites with its unit.

old_proof.text: If $Q$ is an equivariant module sheaf and $v:P\to Q$ an equivariant presheaf map, the module-sheafification adjunction [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives a unique $R$-linear extension $v^\#:A\to Q$. It is equivariant: the two maps $K\times A\to Q$ expressing equivariance are equal after composition with $K\times P\to K\times A$, by equivariance of $v$. This last map is a set-sheafification unit by product preservation [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] and the underlying-set identification [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], so its universal property forces equality. Thus $A$ with the induced action is the reflection of $P$ into equivariant sheaves, with the same unit and underlying module sheafification.

old_proof.text: Apply the equivalences of steps 4--6 to this reflection. For every $R_K$-module sheaf $N$, maps $E(P)\to N$ correspond to equivariant presheaf maps $P\to E^{-1}N$, which by step 8 extend uniquely to maps $A\to E^{-1}N$, hence to maps $E(A)\to N$. Therefore $E(P)\to E(A)$ has precisely the module-sheafification universal property on $C_K$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The canonical isomorphism from the sheafification of $E(P)$ to $E(A)$ is the unique one commuting with the unit. Restriction along $(f,1)$ is consequently the asserted sheafification comparison, natural in $P$; equivariance is part of the same isomorphism.

old_proof.text: For an equivariant map $M\to N$, its sectionwise kernel is stable under $K(U)$ since the map is equivariant. It is the underlying kernel sheaf on $C$ and has the kernel universal property among equivariant maps by restricting their images. The sectionwise cokernel $P(U)=N(U)/\operatorname{im}M(U)$ inherits the linear $K(U)$-action and restriction maps. Its module sheafification on $C$, with the action of step 7, is the equivariant cokernel: maps killing $M$ factor uniquely first through the quotient presheaf and then, equivariantly by step 8, through its sheafification. The formulas agree with the ordinary module kernels and cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so forgetting creates both. Finally the equivalence changes no section modules: a module sheaf on $C_K$ has zero restriction exactly when every section module is zero, which is exactly the zero module sheaf on $C_K$. This also covers the trivial group, the zero ring, and objects admitting empty covers.
